# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.
I'll explore the codebase to locate the transaction-categorization enrichment path and the fixtures behind these RC 2.14 regressions.

# Transaction Enrichment / Categorization — Codebase Report

## 1. Overall project structure

There is **no README**. This is a Flask microservice that categorizes Indian bank statement transactions.

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/Dockerfile` | Python 3.9 image; gunicorn on `:9898` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/setup.py` | Package install (`Flask`, `pandas`, `fuzzywuzzy`, etc.) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py` | Flask app bootstrap |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | HTTP API + bank dispatch pipeline |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` | **Per-bank** category + `partyName` extractors (~35 banks) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/` | Shared post-processing |

**Git history:** single commit `047782b import codebase` (2026-07-15). No multi-commit history of fixes. Canara/PNB show newer mtimes but same import commit.

**No tests, fixtures, baselines, golden files, or sample JSON/CSV** exist in-repo (`.gitignore` even ignores `*.csv`).

---

## 2. Where enrichment / categorization lives

### API entry

- `POST /categorizeTransaction` — main pipeline  
- `POST /recurrentTransactions` — recurrence helper  
- `GET /` — health  

**File:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`  
**Function:** `categorizeTransaction()` (≈L69–936)

### Pipeline (same for every bank)

```
request JSON
  → AppUtil.clean_input_df()
  → categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)   # BankScripts/*
  → [CC only] card_clean_names + card_purpose
  → purpose()                 # subcategory / merchant-ish purpose
  → clean_names()             # merchant canonical names
  → [if accountHolder] internal_payment()
  → [SAVING] salary_detection()
  → [if isPFMEnabled] pfm_categorization() + simple_description()
  → JSON response
```

### Key functions / files

| Concern | Path | Function |
|---------|------|----------|
| Bank category + counterparty | `BankScripts/<Bank>.py` | `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` |
| Purpose / subcategory | `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | `purpose` |
| Merchant name cleanup | `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | `clean_names` |
| CC names/purpose | `CardCleanNames.py`, `CardPurpose.py` | `card_clean_names`, `card_purpose` |
| Self-transfers | `InternalPayment.py` | `internal_payment` |
| Salary | `SalaryDetection.py` | `salary_detection` |
| PFM buckets | `PFMCategorization.py` | `pfm_categorization` |
| Display text | `SimpleDescription.py` | `simple_description` |
| Shared regex | `BankRegexConstants.py`, `RegexConstants.py` | module constants |
| Category enums | `TransactionCategoryEnums.py`, `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` | Enum classes |
| Field helpers | `AppUtil.py` | `sep_by_`, `sep_by_dash`, `py_extract`, `clean_input_df` |

### Bank script pattern (universal)

Each bank script does:

1. **Category:** ordered `np.select` on `description` / `remark` / `amount` / `type` → `transactionCategory` (default **`TRANSFER`**)
2. **Subcategory / merchantType** (optional)
3. **partyName:** slash/dash/colon slice extractors → title-case → cleanup pass → `party2` (spaces stripped)

---

## 3. How categories and counterparty names are derived

### Categories

- Pure **regex / keyword rules** on narration (`description`) and sometimes `remark`
- **First match wins** via `np.select` condition order
- Unmatched → **`TRANSFER`**
- Enums map codes like `CHEQUE_PAID` → display `"Cheque"`, `UPI` → `"UPI"`, etc.

### Counterparty (`partyName`)

- Split narration by `/`, `-`, `:`, `*`, etc. (`AppUtil.sep_by_*`)
- Bank-specific index into tokens (e.g. UPI field 3, NEFT field after UTR)
- Cleanup: blank `NA`, pure numbers, IFSC-like tokens, gateway junk
- Then `clean_names()` rewrites known merchants (large rule table)

### Account verification

Narration keywords + small amount gates, e.g.:

- Shared `BANK_VER` / `BANK_VERIF` / bank-specific `ACC_VERIFY_*` in `BankRegexConstants.py`
- Typical amounts: `eq(1)`, `isin([1,-1])`, `lt(2)`
- **Canara bug:** `amount.lt(1)` never matches a ₹1 penny drop

---

## 4. Test fixtures

**None in this repository.** No `tests/`, no fixtures for cheques / transfers / UPI / verification, no baseline/regression harness.

Illustrative **synthetic** cases you can use against the live rules (not repo files):

### F-1 — Cheque debit, bare number only → TRANSFER

Many banks treat `remark` as cheque number:

```python
# Works on Axis/PNB/Kotak/YES/…  — MISSING on Canara/SBI/ICICI/HDFC debit bare-number, etc.
{"description": "TO TRF", "remark": "001234", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 5000}
# Expected: CHEQUE_PAID
# Canara: falls through → TRANSFER (no remark cheque rule)
```

### F-2 — `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → clearing tag as name

```python
{"description": "CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 10000, "remark": ""}
# Canara: category CHEQUE_PAID (chq keyword), partyName = "Micr Clg"  (dash index 1)
# HDFC: category CHEQUE_PAID; CHQ PAID- uses dash index 3 (empty); later blanks "Micr Clg"
```

### F-3 — Inbound electronic credit, blank counterparty

```python
# ICICI-style NEFT where slash layout doesn't match extractors
{"description": "NEFT-SBIN123456789-SOME COMPANY PVT LTD", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 25000}
# Rules take sep_by_dash(...,2,3); wrong segment → blanked by numeric/junk cleanup
```

### F-4 — P2P UPI credit → bare RRN

```python
# Canara / ICICI-style
{"description": "UPI/CR/312345678901/RAVI KUMAR/SBIN/Payment", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 500}
# Canara: ^UPI/[CD]R → slash index 2 → "312345678901"
# Cleanup blanks ^[0-9]{5,} → empty OR leaves short refs depending on bank
```

### F-5 — Account verification → TRANSFER

```python
{"description": "IMPS Txn Account Verification Penny Drop", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 1}
# Canara: BANK_VERIF matches text BUT amount.lt(1) is False for 1.0 → TRANSFER
# HDFC: amount.lt(2) + BANK_VER → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION
```

---

## 5. Baseline / regression test setup

**Does not exist.**

How to exercise manually:

```bash
cd /app/categorizationapp
pip3 install -e .
# Run API
gunicorn -w 1 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
# or
python -m categorizationapp   # if __main__ path used
```

```bash
curl -s localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "bank": "CANARA_BANK",
  "acc_type": "SAVING",
  "accountUID": "t1",
  "accountHolder": "",
  "isPFMEnabled": false,
  "transactions": [{
    "description": "CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR",
    "remark": "",
    "type": "DEBIT",
    "amount": 10000,
    "balanceAfterTransaction": 0,
    "transactionDate": "2024-01-01"
  }]
}'
```

Bank string must match `Controller` branches (`CANARA_BANK`, `PNB`, `HDFC`, `ICICI`, `SBI`, …). Unknown bank → `"Bank Not Found."`

There is no pytest/unittest layout to “run tests.”

---

## 6. Findings F-1 … F-5 mapped to code

### F-1: Cheque debit with bare number note → generic TRANSFER

**Root cause:** Cheque number often lives only in `remark` (`^[0-9]{3,6}$`). Banks **without** that rule default to `TRANSFER`.

**Has bare-number remark → cheque**

- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py` L58–59  
- `PNB.py` L60–61 (debit exactly 5 digits; credit 5–6)  
- `Kotak.py` L65–67, `YES.py` L52–53, `UCO.py` L44–45, `BOB.py` L70, `BOM` L73–74, `RBL.py` L49–50, `Indusind.py` L64, etc.

**Missing bare-number remark cheque (gap)**

Including: **`Canara.py`**, SBI, ICICI, Central, Federal, IDFC, IDBI, Syndicate, Standard Chartered, …

**Canara** only classifies cheque via narration keywords (`chq|cheque|to clg|by clg`) — L70–71. Bare cheque number in remark alone → **TRANSFER**.

Also note **PNB** debit rule is `^[0-9]{5}$` only — 4- or 6-digit cheque numbers miss.

---

### F-2: `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → counterparty = clearing tag

**Canara** (`Canara.py` L163–166):

```python
[... "Chq Paid-Home Clearing-", ...], sep_by_dash(..., 2, 3)],  # name OK
[... "^CHQ PAID-", ...], sep_by_dash(..., 1, 2)],               # ← takes "MICR CLG"
[... "^To Clg :", ...], ...
```

For `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`, dash tokens =  
`["CHQ PAID", "MICR CLG", "RAVI KUMAR"]` → index **1** = **`MICR CLG`**.

Home Clearing uses index 2 (name); **MICR CLG is not special-cased**.

**HDFC** (`HDFC.py`):

- L163: `CHQ PAID-` → `sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)` (wrong for 2-dash MICR CLG form → empty)
- Patterns `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` = `CHQ PAID-MICR CTS` only — **not** `MICR CLG`  
  (`BankRegexConstants.py` L81–90)
- L260: blanks party if `Micr Clg|Chq Paid` — wipes tag but **does not recover name**

**Central** L74: `CHQ PAID-` → dash index 2 — better for this shape.

---

### F-3: Inbound electronic-transfer credits → blank counterparty

Party extraction is brittle slash/dash indexing. Gaps:

| Bank | File | Issue |
|------|------|--------|
| ICICI | `ICICI.py` L152–158, L206–207, L233 | `^NEFT-` takes dash field 2; many inbound formats put name elsewhere; L233 blanks `[0-9]{6,}` and short tokens |
| Canara | `Canara.py` L116–121 | Several NEFT layouts; unmatched → `""` |
| HDFC | `HDFC.py` L157–162 | Dash-based NEFT/IMPS; inbound variants miss |
| PNB | `PNB.py` L96–110 | Many NEFT_IN patterns; residual formats still blank |

ICICI even has a **commented-out** better INF/NEFT extractor (L153).

After extract, cleanup often zeros party when the wrong token is a UTR/IFSC/number.

---

### F-4: P2P instant-payment credit → bare reference number

**Canara** L107–109:

```python
"^UPI/0" + 7 slashes → field 7
"^UPI/[CD]R" → sep_by_(..., 2, 3)   # often the RRN/ref after CR/DR
"UPV/DR/" → field 3
```

Then L174 blanks `^[0-9]{5,}` — so pure long refs become empty, not names. Short refs or alphanumeric RRNs can remain as “name.”

**ICICI** L139: UPI always `sep_by_(..., 3, 4)` — wrong for formats where field 3 is RRN.  
L233 blanks long pure-numeric party names (after the fact).

**PNB** has richer P2A/P2M/P2V handling (L152–156) but generic UPI without those tags can still grab the wrong field.

**SBI** L99: UPI → field 3 only.

---

### F-5: Small account-verification deposit → ordinary TRANSFER

**Smoking gun — Canara** L19:

```python
... BANK_VERIF ... & transactions.amount.lt(1) , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"
```

₹1 (and ₹1.0) fails `lt(1)`. Typical penny-drop never categorizes as verification → **TRANSFER**.

`BANK_VERIF` (`BankRegexConstants.py` L321) is broad (`verif|pennyd|valida|IMPS Txn|FUND TRANS|…`) but the amount gate kills it.

Compare:

| Bank | Gate |
|------|------|
| HDFC | `amount.lt(2)` |
| PNB / RBL | `amount.lt(2)` |
| ICICI / Axis / most PSUs | `isin([1,-1])` or `eq(1)` |
| **Canara** | **`lt(1)` ← broken** |
| Kotak | Only narrow narrations + `eq(1)` |
| BOM / Indusind | string `"1"` in `isin` (type risk if amount is numeric) |

Phrase “is this account live” is **not** in any verification regex; only generic verif/penny/validation tokens.

Purpose.py L165 also maps `LOAN` subcategory + amount ±1 → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` (secondary path).

---

## Obvious bugs / pattern gaps (summary)

1. **Canara `amount.lt(1)`** for account verification — almost certainly should be `lt(2)` / `eq(1)` / `isin([1,-1])` (`Canara.py:19`).
2. **Canara `^CHQ PAID-` party extract uses dash index 1** — yields `MICR CLG` instead of payee (`Canara.py:165`); needs MICR/Home-Clearing-style index 2+ and/or strip clearing tokens.
3. **No remark-as-cheque-number rule on Canara** (and many other banks) → F-1.
4. **HDFC MICR CLG** not in `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*`; generic `CHQ PAID-` index wrong; cleanup drops tag without recovering name (`HDFC.py` + `BankRegexConstants.py`).
5. **UPI field-index one-size-fits-all** frequently selects RRN (Canara `UPI/[CD]R` field 2; ICICI field 3).
6. **Inbound NEFT/IMPS** heavily format-dependent; ICICI commented extractor; numeric cleanup erases wrong picks → blank party (F-3).
7. **`np.select` first-match** + default `TRANSFER` means any missed keyword is a silent miscategorization.
8. **No automated regression** — findings cannot be locked without adding fixtures outside this tree.
9. **BOM/Indusind** use `amount.isin(["1","-1"])` (strings) while amounts are numeric — verification may never fire.
10. **Controller** is a huge copy-pasted if/elif per bank — easy to fix one bank and leave siblings broken.

---

## How categories relate to your five findings

| Finding | Primary location | Expected category | Actual if broken |
|---------|------------------|-------------------|------------------|
| F-1 | BankScripts remark rules (missing on Canara et al.) | `CHEQUE_PAID` | `TRANSFER` |
| F-2 | Canara L165; HDFC L163/L260 + CHQ patterns | `CHEQUE_PAID` + name | `CHEQUE_PAID` + `Micr Clg` / blank |
| F-3 | NEFT/IMPS party blocks per bank | `NEFT`/`IMPS`/`RTGS` + name | category OK, `partyName=""` |
| F-4 | UPI party slash indices + numeric cleanup | `UPI` + sender | `UPI` + RRN or blank |
| F-5 | Canara L19 `amount.lt(1)`; keyword lists | `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` | `TRANSFER` |

---

## Recent changes

Only history available: **one bulk import**. No diffs that specifically fix F-1–F-5. Treat Canara/PNB as high-signal areas for those narration styles, but the bugs above are visible in current source without git blame trails.

If you want next steps in-repo: add a small pytest suite calling `categorize_Canara_transactions` / `categorize_HDFC_transactions` with the synthetic rows above and assert `transactionCategory` + `partyName`.

steps.reasoning_content:
Interesting findings from the tests:
The Canara ruleset is clearly missing a couple of edge-case patterns that HDFC already handles. The “is this account live” credit is being caught by HDFC’s BANK_VERIF because it contains the substring “Accou” (from “account”), but Canara’s BANK_VERIF only has “Account va / BANK ACCOU” which doesn’t overlap with “account l” once case-insensitive matching is applied. Switching the amount check from lt(1) to lt(2) would fix F5 immediately.

For F4 the format is inconsistent across banks: when the reference number comes first (UPI/CR/312345 678901/RAVI KUMAR) Canara’s rule takes index 2 which is numeric and blanks it, whereas ICICI’s rule takes index 3 which is the name.

| Finding | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| **F-1** | Bare remark cheque numbers (`^[0-9]{3,6}$`) → `CHEQUE_PAID` / `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` |

| **F-3** | NEFT/IMPS credit name from correct field (not UTR/RRN/`CREDIT`) |
| **F-4** | `UPI/[CD]R/<rrn>/name` takes name when field 2 is numeric |
| **F-5** | Account verification amount gate `lt(1)` → `lt(2)` so ₹1 penny-drops match |
